title: Capacity surge cascade — customer comms, timeline, and action tracker
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Summary: On 2026-03-08 we observed a capacity surge cascade in us-west that led to degraded performance (elevated tail latency) and intermittent 503s for a subset of hosted customers. Root cause: a regression in the autoscaler control loop that over-provisioned small GPU instances under a specific synthetic traffic pattern and triggered a downstream scheduling backlog. This ticket tracks customer-facing communications, the consolidated incident timeline for the status page, and the postmortem action items necessary to prevent recurrence.

Why this ticket exists: previous postmortem artifacts were split across PRs and a draft Confluence page; this ticket centralizes the communications plan, assigns owners for customer follow-ups, and turns the RCA into concrete engineering tasks with timelines.

Audience: customer success, support, PMs, oncall eng, infra, and docs.
timeline: 2026-03-08 02:14 UTC: First anomaly detected by autoscaler health metric (rate-of-change of active pods).
2026-03-08 02:19 UTC: Pager duty triggered for infra-oncall (high tail latency, 5% 503s across us-west).
2026-03-08 02:27 UTC: Oncall escalated to serving-runtime team. Initial mitigation: temporarily increased global scheduled capacity to absorb backlog.
2026-03-08 02:45 UTC: Partial restoration of request latency for most customers; some long-running KV cache thrash persisted.
2026-03-08 03:10 UTC: Root-cause hypothesis formed: autoscaler control loop mis-evaluated eviction pressure when synthetic bursts hit small instance types.
2026-03-08 04:00 UTC: Emergency rollback of autoscaler change deployed (revert PR #4091) which removed the regression; full service recovery by 04:12 UTC.
2026-03-09: Initial status page update posted (customer notification) and support playbook circulated to CS and SRE.
2026-03-10: Postmortem draft started; consolidated logs and k8s scheduling traces imported to the incident doc.

resolution_summary:
Immediate mitigation: rolled back autoscaler change (PR #4091) and temporarily increased scheduled capacity to clear the backlog. Result: traffic normalized and 503s fell to baseline within ~1 hour after rollback. Root cause: regression in control loop logic that underestimated transient allocation lag for small GPU instance types under bursty synthetic traffic.

Impact: elevated tail latency and intermittent 503s for a subset of hosted customers in us-west for ~1h 58m, high business impact for latency-sensitive customers.

Lessons learned: instrument autoscaler decision path with end-to-end latency signals, add synthetic-burst Canary tests, and implement conservative guardrails when scaling-down under high rate-of-change windows.
